extraction.Name: Susie Garnett
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her allotment for the reason that she did not wish to pay taxes, but was advised by the Indian Agency that the patent would be forced upon her, and that she would have taxes to pay any way; so she accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: never mortgaged her land; but that, in 1921, she sold 240 acres to Mr. Roy Thomas, of Brannan, South Dakota, receiving $3000.00 cash; that this left her 80 acres of her 320 acre allotment, which was finally taken for taxes; and that she now owns no land
extraction.Buyer: Mr. Roy Thomas, of Brannan, South Dakota, for $3000.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: 80 acres of her 320 acre allotment was finally taken for taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: supports herself by working at household duties for other people, whenever she can obtain work; and that her income is small for her needs
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; health is fairly good, except that she is bothered badly with rheumatism at times; unmarried; no one contributes to her support, nor she to no one else; has never received any aid from the County or United States Government; allotment was 320 acres; document number 286; County of Shannon, State of South Dakota; sworn November 14, 1928 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 49 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
